newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan seeds 38 percent of crop by Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan seeds 38 percent of crop by Sunday.

text.p: Saskatchewan farmers seeded 38 percent of 1997 crops compared to six percent at the same time last year and ahead of the five-year average of 35 percent, Saskatchewan Agriculture said in its weekly crop report.
"Seeding varies across the province with the southern grainbelt reporting the most progress at 49 percent," it said.
Central Saskatchewan seeded 36 percent of its crops by May 18 while northern Saskatchewan seeded 19 percent of crops.
Sixty-eight percent of lentils were seeded, 61 percent of durum wheat, 50 percent of peas and 43 percent of spring wheat was planted.
Windy weather deteriorated top soil moisture but the majority of the province reported good moisture conditions. Many southern and central areas reported fair to poor moisture conditions.
Winterkill was reported on nine percent of winter wheat and eight percent of fall rye.
There were reports of bottlenecks in fertilizer supplies in the central and northern grainbelts as well as some chemical shortages.
The south saw an average of less than 1 mm of rain, the central region saw an average 4 mm and the north saw 11 mm.
